access.edition_or_version: French text public domain; standard editions and translations widely available. Claims use essay locators (I.26, III.13), which are edition-stable, not page numbers.

tone_mechanisms_observed: the self as material of a trial: general questions tested against the essayist's own habits and body
provisional modality and self-questioning; conclusions suspended rather than proven
visible revision across the 1580/1588/1595 edition layers
outward question, inward evidence: digression licensed, judgment held open under a questioning motto
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person essayistic 'I' used as evidence, watched as it thinks — a controlled double stance.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Shifts between present-tense self-observation and past-tense anecdote; the unit of structure is the attempt (essai), not the argument, and the essay's end is a suspension, not a proof.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Uneven accumulative periods; digressive hypotaxis — the main clause abandoned mid-sentence for an aside, then resumed; pacing follows the movement of attention rather than plot.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Close on the act of thinking but ironized: the essayist observes himself observing, an inbuilt slight step back.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Classical allusion used as mirror rather than ornament; analogy drawn from ordinary bodily experience; first-person inventory immediately qualified by personal counter-example and concessive connectives.
mechanics.copyright_note: Public domain. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
